logical_uniform_coverage.structurally_unmappable_reason: the Xbox disc stores each jersey/helmet/arm digit as its own texture and the nameplate as a 1024x32 strip; the PS2 disc packs each digit family into one atlas and has no indexed texture at the nameplate chunk, so no GS hash names these targets

demo_team.chosen_reason: no kit has a shipped row for all eight of its mappable components. The PS2 disc shares torso, sleeve, pants and helmet art across a team's era variants -- three Bills away kits carry one sleeve texture -- so those textures belong to no single logical target and the export service would refuse to attribute a file written under one. WP7 should witness the components that did map on the kit named in logical.best_covered_kit, and treat a fully-mappable kit as work for a later slice that resolves shared art rather than as a blocker here.
criteria: every mappable component of the kit has a shipped manifest row under the logical id a Studio edit actually carries
the kit is on screen in a GS dump that already exists on the rig, so the render can be witnessed by dump replay
demo_team.method: the 634 Xbox uniform selectors and their 39 components come from the hash-pinned compatibility reports; a component is mapped when the manifest names at least one PCSX2 replacement for its logical id. Thirty-one of the 39 (the ten digits of each family, plus the nameplate) have no PS2 counterpart texture at all and are excluded from 'fully mappable' -- see counts.logical_uniform_coverage

physical.note: the texture-level view: which of a selector's tset children resolve to a unique manifest row. Kept as supporting evidence; the logical view above is what an export actually needs

claim:superseded_by_logical_uniform_id.reason: the texture is also named by a logical uniform target, and the logical id is the one a Studio uniform edit carries; publishing both would make the export service call the file unattributable and skip it under either name

claim:texture_shared_by_several_uniform_.reason: several uniform kits share this one PS2 texture, so no single logical target owns it; editing one kit would repaint the others

fanout:mixed.reason: the identity is proved but the name resolves to more than one Xbox asset in the mixed namespace

fanout:p8.reason: the identity is proved but the name resolves to more than one Xbox asset in the p8 namespace

fanout:scene.reason: the identity is proved but the name resolves to more than one Xbox asset in the scene namespace

fanout:tset.reason: the identity is proved but the name resolves to more than one Xbox asset in the tset namespace

no_xbox_id.reason: both hashes reproduce but the PS2 resource name has no counterpart on the Xbox disc

tex0_only.reason: the level-0 pixel hash reproduces but no CLUT candidate matches the palette hash in the filename; the identity is unproved and never ships

unexplained.reason: a canonical identity in the reference pack that no disc texture reproduces under any layout; open, unbudgeted
